text:
kai: Quick q — we're rolling out a change to rerank fanout and billing. Proposal: charge 'score_units' per candidate scored and add explicit 'score_kind' in the response so consumers know semantics. Thoughts?

anna: +1 to explicit units. I think we should expose X-Score-Units header and emit score_units in telemetry. Console should show a stacked breakdown by model, cache savings, and fallbacks.

mike: Compatibility note: older clients expect just a scores array. We should keep scores as-is and add an optional scoring_meta field. Also define default score_kind (logit vs normalized) — we need to pick one to avoid silent regressions.

sam: @mike agree. Suggest enum score_kind: ["raw_logit","softmax_prob","normalized"], default to "normalized" so most UXs don't break. Telemetry should emit fanout_count and primary_model.

kai: Rough envelope example (thinking aloud):

```json
{
  "scores": [0.72, 0.31, 0.12],
  "score_kind": "normalized",
  "scoring_meta": [
    {"model": "rwd-v1", "units": 2},
    {"model": "rwd-v1", "units": 2},
    {"model": "rwd-v2", "units": 1}
  ]
}
```

Would that work?

anna: Need per-candidate model attribution + fallback flag: scoring_meta[i].fallback = true if candidate was produced by a degraded model. Also include kv_cache_hit flag.

mike: Payload size perf concern. Per-candidate objects blow up responses. Maybe compress to parallel arrays to keep envelope small: score_models: ["rwd-v1","rwd-v1","rwd-v2"], score_units: [2,2,1], score_fallback: [false,false,true].

sam: For console UX: show "expected token cost" next to each rerank route and a signal when fanout spikes above route budget. Add a rollout knob to cap fanout per route to protect cost-sensitive workloads.

kai: Routing policy question: when capacity constrained, do we prefer cheaper model variants or just reduce fanout? Current policy is "min-latency then fallback", but for non-interactive batch jobs maybe we want "min-cost" by default. Need a per-route policy toggle.

anna: Yeah — route-level policy toggle in console: latency | cost | reliability. Also add knobs for max_candidates and max_fanout, with clear wording about billing implications.

mike: Billing sanity: charge units after caching. If KV cache hit avoids scoring, we shouldn't bill. Telemetry must include kv_cache_hit boolean per candidate and a post-cache unit count metric.

sam: Edge-case: third-party model vendors report different unit semantics. Normalization proposal: each model registers a model_unit_weight in metadata so the aggregator multiplies by units to compute billing. Telemetry tag keys: route, team, model_variant. Metric names: rerank.fanout.count, rerank.score.units, rerank.kv_hits.

kai: Plan: I'll draft an API PR that adds optional scoring_meta (parallel arrays form) + emits telemetry events: rerank.fanout and rerank.kv_hits. Then a small console mock for stacked cost bars and a route-level policy toggle. Anyone object?

anna: :thumbsup: include example metric names and tag schema in the PR description.

mike: Add integration tests ensuring old clients can still parse just "scores". Also add perf benchmarks for payload size. Marking P1 for next sprint if infra signs off.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled 2026-05-03T08:00Z for api/rerank v2. Rolling update policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100%.

sam: Noted — please include a canary metric in the console showing cost delta vs baseline (so we can detect cost regressions during rollout).

kai: Thanks all. I'll open the PR and attach a Figma mock for console UX. Will tag infra and billing.

(ending thread)
